# Celorga

Remote Codex over SSH destinations reuse an existing Codex or `~/.ssh/config` host alias, start Codex's managed app-server daemon on that machine, and attach to its private Unix socket through SSH. They require no separately maintained WebSocket tunnel, listener, TLS certificate, or bearer token. If the Mac sleeps or the SSH stream drops after a turn starts, the daemon keeps owning that turn; Celorga reconnects and reads the same turn after wake without submitting the message twice. Client-hosted workspace tools wait until the Mac is available again. Legacy WebSocket Codex destinations remain compatible but are hidden from normal destination setup.

> Celorga is a local-first knowledge compiler and runtime for Org-shaped plain text. Ordinary .org files are canonical; agendas, graph data, context packets, reports, editor behavior, apps, and websites derive from the shared compiler/runtime.

After enabling Settings → General → Experimental features (off by default), Mac direct-provider destinations can opt into workspace tools through a bundled TypeScript foreground executor. It uses the app's existing Node runtime and offers bounded corpus search, effective-text reads, and SHA-bound preview/apply tools. Every patch requires native user review; secondary authorized corpora are read-only. Existing destinations keep tools disabled. The prototype is text-only, delivers complete model steps, and does not automatically resume an interrupted tool loop. It introduces no independent corpus database or scheduler.

Installed agents should begin with:

    celorga agent capabilities
    celorga --help
    celorga agent --help

The first command emits the machine-readable `celorga:capabilities:v1` manifest. Mutating commands generally preview unless `--apply` is provided. Preserve citations, IDs, provenance, and review state; place generated work in `views/` or `compiled/` before promotion into canonical notes.

Corpus extensions use one `celorga plugin` system; there is no separate native-app plugin ABI. Portable Git source intent lives in `celorga.json`; the corpus plugin lock file pins an exact commit, validated manifest, and SHA-256 package hash; the machine-wide content store deduplicates identical packages. GitHub HTTPS URLs, `github:OWNER/REPOSITORY`, general Git URLs, file URLs, local checkouts, refs, and repository subdirectories are supported. `plugin add` and `plugin update` are the only operations that move mutable refs; `plugin sync` reproduces the lock. Downloaded code is inert until its exact content hash is trusted locally. V1 packages contribute explicit CLI commands, static templates, document renderers shared by CLI HTML export and Celorga, context-aware actions for a selected note, heading, thread, run, or approval (`celorga plugin actions`, `celorga plugin action run`), and lifecycle hooks for events such as `run.blocked`, `run.completed`, `approval.requested`, and `thread.reply-received` (`celorga plugin hooks dispatch --apply`). Actions and hooks run under a macOS sandbox without corpus write access and return proposals (exact-text edits, files under `views/`, chat posts, run comments) that stay pending in `.celorga/plugin-proposals/` until a person applies them with `celorga plugin proposals apply ID --apply` or Celorga's review sheet. Trusted processes have user-level file and network access; renderer output is separately confined to a sandboxed opaque-origin iframe with a deny-by-default content policy. Use `plugin trust ID --revoke --apply` to stop executing a hash.

Publishing includes disclosure-safe single-document destinations, ordinary single-file HTML, multi-file HTML projects, and Beamer-compatible presentations. `celorga publish document --file REPORT.org --to web --out-dir DIR` previews a sealed web bundle; `--line N` selects one subtree. The same safe projection can produce a safe Beamer PDF with `--to beamer-pdf`, an editable Google Doc with `--to google-docs`, a Google Slides deck with `--to google-slides`, a Google Sheets workbook with `--to google-sheets`, or a Google Drive PDF with `--to google-drive-pdf`. Docs, Slides, and Sheets use deterministic DOCX, ODP, and ODS imports; Sheets create one tab per Org table. Publishing strips private Org metadata, internal links, comments, raw HTML, and runtime data before any destination receives content. A static bundle does not enforce authentication; the selected host owns public, secret-link, or per-person access, while Google Drive owns permissions for its files. Use `celorga export beamer --file TALK.org` when author-controlled TeX is intentional: it previews TeX generation, `--apply` writes it, and `--pdf` compiles through `pdflatex` (or the command selected by `--latex-engine`). Presentation structure is compiled from the shared Org AST; legacy `BEAMER_*` properties and backend-neutral `SLIDE_*` properties map into the same presentation model.

Explicit color presentation uses preserved custom links rather than inferred column names: `[[color:red][urgent]]` binds foreground, `[[color:bg=yellow][review]]` binds background, and `[[color:fg=white;bg=#b42318][blocked]]` binds both. These non-navigating spans work in ordinary inline content and AI chat; a sole binding in a table cell applies to the whole cell. Invalid or arbitrary CSS remains an ordinary link.

Org pipe tables can carry structured `#+TBLFM:` spreadsheet formulas. `celorga table recalculate --file FILE` previews safe deterministic evaluation and `--apply` writes changed cells atomically. The shared renderer, Mac app, CLI, LSP, VS Code, Vim, and Tree-sitter surfaces recognize the same formula lines. Arithmetic, relative/absolute references, ranges, vector aggregates, numeric formats, and duration modes are supported; Emacs Lisp, remote tables, and arbitrary Calc extensions remain lossless but are never executed.

The native Celorga app for macOS consumes that shared presentation classification to select document or slide preview automatically per file, while retaining an explicit per-file override. Its compiled-PDF view supports slide-number navigation, previous/next and first/last keyboard movement, and fit-relative zoom without recompiling the deck.

The native Celorga app for macOS renders corpus HTML files as web pages (with a source toggle and live reload) and opens clicked web links as pages in the detail pane with document back/forward history, including local development servers such as `localhost:5173` and folders served read-only over loopback http. Its Source editor highlights code, markup, config, and data files natively from the shared highlighter's generated language table.

Every loaded Org node in the native Celorga app for macOS shows an editable entity-type badge. Common and custom choices are persisted as a `CELORGA_ENTITY_TYPE` property on the file or heading. Full-page people, companies, and projects include a bounded action-item panel backed by `celorga query actions`. The deterministic query combines TODOs directly linked or related through entity properties with TODOs inherited from containing meetings that link to the entity, plus dated recent completions. It uses the incremental corpus cache and does not invoke an agent or generate a node brief.

`celorga workspace agent-state --dir CORPUS --json` batches the run, workflow, goal, and agent-profile lists for one corpus, preserving each list envelope with independent section errors and timings.

Portable corpus identity lives in the root `celorga.json`. Use `celorga corpus show|validate|init` before mounting a corpus for team or agent use. `celorga workspace agenda|search` can combine read-only results from repeatable, explicitly named `--mount` paths and attaches corpus identity to every result. Writes remain scoped to the active corpus; an agent must not inherit all human-visible mounts by convenience.

Portable external-source intent may also live in `celorga.json`, but credentials and machine paths must not. Use `celorga source list|doctor|status|bind|schedule|import|sync` to orchestrate the external `slacrawl` and `notcrawl` binaries, `celorga source add PROFILE --source-json JSON [--update]` to create or update a validated, secret-free profile of any type (slack, notion, email), and `celorga source add-email PROFILE --host HOST --username USER` for IMAP email profiles that Celorga syncs itself (read-only EXAMINE/BODY.PEEK, machine-local UID cursor, password from `CELORGA_EMAIL_PASSWORD`, a `--password-env`/`--password-command` binding, or the Celorga app's Keychain storage; never in the corpus). `source import` previews bounded raw captures and review-required Org packets; `source sync PROFILE --ingest --apply` refreshes and stages them. A profile may declare a validated interval or daily schedule; `source schedule` previews or atomically applies cadence changes and pause/resume state. The Mac app exposes Run Now and per-connector schedule controls, executes due schedules while running, catches up after wake or launch, and keeps last-attempt/next-run/error state local to that machine. Bindings live outside the corpus under the machine's Celorga index home, and the Mac app adds or configures every source type from one form and keeps each type's token or password in Keychain, so clients can invoke the same corpus profile with independent local authorization.

The native Celorga app for macOS also exposes a discoverable chat slash-command layer. Its local commands reuse shared search, backlink, lint, render, and publish semantics; agent-assisted `/brief` and `/summarize` receive selected source context with citations. User-invocable skills in the active corpus's `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` are loaded into autocomplete locally, labeled as skills, and forwarded to either the OpenClaw or Codex runtime without requiring Gateway discovery. When the live OpenClaw Gateway supports `commands.list`, its runtime-native, skill, and plugin commands for the selected agent are also merged into autocomplete and forwarded unchanged through `chat.send`; they do not use HTTP compatibility. Gateway progress intentionally exposed by the provider is stored with the assistant reply, while repetitive tool completion events are grouped into a compact work log. See Celorga reference for details.

The Mac Files surface and quick open include CSV files. Opening a local CSV link from rendered Org content or AI chat keeps it inside the detail pane, where table and raw-text modes share the app's ordinary autosave, Command-S, stale-write protection, and file undo behavior. CSV data remains an ordinary file and is excluded from Org semantic indexing.

The Mac app can optionally pair as a narrow local-edit node as well as an operator UI. With this setting enabled and connected, chat turns use the plugin's typed workspace read, patch-preview, and patch-apply node commands instead of Gateway filesystem writes. Reads include the effective selected editor draft; previews are bound to SHA-256 inputs; apply rechecks them, stays inside the corpus where the turn began, and supplies the exact per-turn change summary. The node exposes no generic shell. This requires the OpenClaw lifecycle plugin's node policy, node-role pairing, and the selected agent's `nodes` tool.

New Mac AI-chat threads choose among named configured destinations. Settings lists only destinations the user has configured; Add Destination creates a draft that becomes available after Save, and Delete removes an unused destination after confirmation. Available adapters include local Codex, Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, and OpenClaw; SSH-hosted Pi or OpenCode; remote Codex; and direct providers. Local Claude Code uses the installed `claude` CLI and its existing Anthropic sign-in, streams `stream-json` replies, resumes Claude sessions, supports attachments, and maps Celorga's Read Only, Workspace Write, and Full Access setting to Claude Code's Plan, Accept Edits, and Bypass Permissions modes. Local Codex continues to use `codex app-server` with ChatGPT subscription authentication and Celorga's reviewed workspace tools. The selected corpus context and authorized roots are captured per turn; secondary corpora remain read-only. Mobile Remote exposes every configured destination. A conversation continues on the host (desktop or headless server) whose runtime last ran it: other hosts hand new messages to it through the synchronized corpus and show its live progress from a presence record, falling back to running the turn themselves when that host is offline. Messages record the originating client, receiving host, and executing host.

Normal Mac Workspace chat turns include a non-secret snapshot of the active corpus's configured Celorga source profiles and general source-discovery guidance. OpenClaw uses `celorga source list/status` and the returned profile IDs, types, scopes, raw zones, and review zones as the authority, searches staged source material as ordinary Org text, and refreshes a matching enabled profile when fresher material is needed. It asks the user about setup only when `celorga source doctor` reports a specific missing machine-local binding or credential.

OpenClaw is currently the deepest native adapter. The repository's `integrations/openclaw` lifecycle plugin records substantial main-agent turns, subagent executions, and cron executions as correlated durable runs. Scheduled workflow executions share a stable logical-work ID but receive distinct numbered attempt records; declared event/fresh-path gates create a safe skipped attempt instead of starting expensive workflow steps when no new signal exists. The plugin preserves available provider/model and usage metadata, records terminal outcome summaries, leaves approval or clarification boundaries open, continues an approved workflow in its correlated chat session, and verifies the Mac app's selected portable corpus identity against its single configured write corpus. Other agents can use the same run/workflow files, cited retrieval, CLI JSON, MCP surfaces, and the packaged general Celorga skill. Install a corpus copy with preview-first `celorga skill install --dir CORPUS`; add `--apply` only after review.

Goals and named workers are portable corpus concepts. `celorga goal` manages `celorga:goal:v1` records under `goals/`; `celorga agent-profile` manages `celorga:agent-profile:v1` records under `agent-profiles/`. OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode are runtimes, not agent profile IDs. Profiles may bind a non-secret runtime identity such as `openclaw:customer-support` or `codex:default`; resolve one with `celorga agent-profile resolve --runtime RUNTIME --runtime-agent-id ID --dir CORPUS --json`. Preserve returned `agentRef` and `goalRef` on `run create`, `workflow run`, or delegated TODO properties. Existing selected-work refs take precedence, `ASSIGNEE` remains only a readable label, and unbound identities must remain unset rather than guessed.

Prompt automations are ordinary `celorga:workflow:v1` files under `workflows/`. `celorga workflow create ID --title TEXT --prompt TEXT --destination-ref ID [--model ID --reasoning-effort LEVEL] [--schedule EXPR --timezone IANA]` creates one, and `workflow due --json` reports the latest missed occurrence while suppressing overlap with an active attempt. The workflow's optional `model` and `reasoningEffort` fields pin each invocation; absent fields use destination/runtime defaults and never inherit interactive-chat overrides. Preview-first `workflow delete ID [--apply]` removes only the definition and preserves prior runs. Celorga's Mac scheduler creates a durable run before sending the resolved prompt to any configured AI destination, including Codex, Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, OpenClaw, or a direct provider. Pi and OpenCode destinations may run locally or over SSH in an explicitly configured remote corpus path. The symbolic destination reference is canonical; credentials remain machine-local, and a missing explicit destination or unsupported pinned reasoning value fails instead of rerouting or being silently ignored. Provider-native clocks are optional adapters over the same file and history.

Durable delegation uses generated run records under `.celorga/runs/` and authored workflow files under the visible `workflows/` directory. Celorga continues to read the legacy early-alpha workflows folder inside the hidden state directory. Discover the interfaces with:

    celorga run --help
    celorga workflow --help
    celorga doctor --dir CORPUS --json
    celorga ledger list account-outreach --eligible --dir CORPUS --json
    celorga ledger resolve account-outreach --identity NAME_OR_EMAIL_OR_DOMAIN --dir CORPUS --json
    celorga approvals --dir CORPUS --recursive --format json
    celorga review list --dir CORPUS --json
    celorga mcp serve --dir CORPUS

The stdio MCP server exposes paginated Org resources, workflow prompts, bounded cited search, stable-ID fetch, context assembly, read-only coordination queries, and three trusted local run/thread mutations. A headless Celorga server can expose only the five read-only tools over bearer-authenticated Streamable HTTP on its Tailscale address. `celorga server token create --name CLIENT --apply` prints a client token once and stores only its SHA-256 hash in machine-local configuration; token, port, origin, and MCP state changes require a restart. Hosted systems still need an authenticated public HTTPS path that can reach this private listener.

Planned upgrades need not interrupt live turns: `celorga server drain` makes a headless server stop accepting turns, hand-offs, and scheduled automations while running turns finish (clients route new turns elsewhere and reclaim pending hand-offs immediately), `celorga server stop|restart --drain` stops or restarts only after that, and `celorga server resume` cancels a drain. The desktop can prefer a server for new agent turns (a detachable client) and offers Quit When Turns Finish. Presence records carry `isDraining`, and `celorga activity hosts` excludes draining hosts from failover.

Explainable activity is derived from structured records, never terminal output. `celorga activity explain [--thread|--run|--workflow ID] --json` returns `celorga:activity-explanation:v1` items with state, reason code and summary, reporting host/runtime/destination, last heartbeat or transition, live/cached/uncertain confidence, and exact blocking approvals (with run, approval ID, and fingerprint), questions, delivery failures, or artifact reviews. `celorga activity hosts --json` classifies Celorga hosts as online, authentication-needed, reconnecting, stale, or offline with failover candidates. `celorga activity events [--since ISO|15m] [--follow] --json` streams `celorga:activity-event:v1` NDJSON for run, approval, thread, workflow, and host transitions. `celorga thread wait ID --until reply|needs-you|idle|working` and `celorga run wait ID --until approval|blocked|needs-you|running|completed|failed|terminal|status:S` check durable state before watching and exit 0 matched, 2 unreachable, 124 timed out.

AI chat automation is also corpus-owned rather than private Mac UI state. `celorga thread list/show` reads the authoritative sharded transcript, retains compatibility with the older single-file transcript, and projects queued operations. `thread settle/reopen`, `thread configure --auto-settle never|SECONDS`, and `thread auto-settle` preview by default; `--apply` queues an immutable operation under `.celorga/ai-chat-inbox/operations/` instead of directly rewriting the transcript. The Mac app drains those operations while running or when the corpus opens, persists each result durably, and then removes its journal file. `thread post THREAD_ID --message TEXT --author NAME --agent-ref AGENT_REF --source REF --idempotency-key KEY` previews an agent-attributed, no-turn background message; `--apply` queues an append-only envelope under `.celorga/ai-chat-inbox/`. The Mac app persists queued posts into the named thread, reopens a settled destination, marks it unread, and follows the normal notification path without invoking or steering an AI runtime, unless `--request-turn AGENT` names shared-room agents that should respond. The CLI rejects that flag for single-agent chats; use preview-first `thread send THREAD_ID --message TEXT --idempotency-key KEY` and then `--apply` to enqueue a user turn through the existing destination queue (MCP `celorga_thread_send`, with `celorga_thread_list` to find thread IDs). Agents hand work to another agent this way rather than creating an automation just to trigger a turn. A busy agent receives a follow-up after its current turn. Sends use `celorga:ai-chat-send-message:v1`; older consumers retain the request as unsupported. The consuming host must have the original destination enabled; missing or changed destinations retain the envelope with an error. JSON `deliveryStatus` distinguishes preview, queued, and delivered messages; `turnStatus` is not-requested or unconfirmed. A queued or delivered request never confirms model execution, and `run start` changes durable run state without dispatching a turn. In a shared room, an agent reply that @mentions another room agent starts that agent's turn; `thread configure ROOM_ID --agent-turn-limit N|default` caps back-to-back agent-requested turns (default 4, 0 turns hand-offs off) before a person replies. Settled threads retain messages, session keys, context, and searchability. Auto-settlement excludes the selected thread plus pinned, unread, or pending threads and threads whose latest delivery is still sending, failed, or interrupted. Empty threads and recovered historical failures remain eligible.

Runs preserve goals, acceptance criteria, cited inputs, plans, risk, provider metadata, budgets, artifacts, approvals, validation, comments, and observable events. Workflow packages declare inputs, capabilities, writes, outputs, triggers, checks, approval boundaries, and compatibility. External MCP/connector data that becomes durable work should be stored as a provenance-bearing snapshot; credentials stay outside the corpus.
Run and workflow writes are guarded and atomic. `celorga run show RUN_ID --with-revision --json` returns the current SHA-256 file revision; pass it back as `--if-revision REVISION` when state crosses a client/request boundary. The CLI and MCP refuse stale revisions, concurrent locks, duplicate creates, and readable run fields that disagree with canonical machine state instead of silently replacing newer source.
On macOS, `celorga thread repair --dir CORPUS --json` previews deterministic chat reconciliation through the built native server worker, without an LLM. `--apply` publishes a repair head while retaining originals; `--if-revision` guards a reviewed preview. `--watch --interval SECONDS --apply` runs serially and skips unchanged chat storage. Build with `npm run build:server` or supply `--executable PATH`. Desktop AI Chat settings and `celorga server chat-repair --interval off|SECONDS` configure background checks, defaulting to 120 seconds. Incomplete tips, corrupt references, and unknown future fields remain recoverable and cause repair to stop; ordinary note conflicts and intentional deletions are not automatically rewritten.

Recurring account workflows must resolve all available stable identities before creating work. Do not proceed through ambiguity or source drift by guessing.
`celorga doctor --machine --json` returns bounded machine evidence, and `celorga doctor --handoff codex|claude|opencode|pi|openclaw [--agent-ref ID] [--apply] [--launch]` hands it and the troubleshoot playbook to the selected agent without the GUI. It previews by default, `--apply` writes only `views/diagnostics/handoffs/`, `--launch` starts the runtime once in the foreground with restricted permissions, and it never schedules a job. `celorga doctor --dir CORPUS --json` is the read-only integrity check for this boundary. It reports contradictory run/approval state, duplicate provider decision keys, conflicting or overlapping recurring attempts, unmanaged OpenClaw cron series, broken projected links, readable-header drift from canonical run state, and likely duplicate open headings. Errors return a nonzero exit code. The doctor never repairs source automatically; inspect its cited evidence and use canonical lifecycle operations or an explicit reviewed source edit.
For account-oriented recurring work, use `celorga ledger` instead of appending global bookkeeping to one agent file. Curated account records live under `notes/LEDGER/accounts/`, one file per account ID; raw exports and provider payloads remain under `raw/`, and generated selections belong in `views/`. Creates, updates, and events preview unless `--apply` is present. Stable identity keys and ledger-wide event idempotency keys prevent duplicate accounts and repeated actions. Link native run approvals by `runId/approvalId`; do not copy their decision status into the ledger. `outreach-sent` requires an external receipt ID and, when approval-linked, an approved canonical decision. Eligibility remains closed after proposal/approval until a sent, canceled, or skipped event settles that outreach cycle. Readable event history and structured event state must agree: `celorga doctor` reports out-of-band drift and later structured writes fail closed instead of erasing it.
`celorga approvals` is the unified pending-decision queue. A `kind=run` item names the exact `runId` and `approvalId` in `.celorga/runs/`, carries the immutable SHA-256 fingerprint of its review material, exposes deterministic provider `decisionKeys` when available, includes the run goal/status and remaining approval count, and must be decided through `celorga run approval-decide --fingerprint FINGERPRINT`. Approval decisions are item-scoped: rejecting or canceling one action leaves sibling approvals pending, and a fully decided boundary resumes with rejected or canceled actions excluded. Recording one approval as completed elsewhere cancels only that approval with an external receipt; it never completes the containing run. `--decision revised` keeps the workflow open for replacement material and requires `--note "Requested changes"` so that work has durable direction. A `kind=headline` item remains an ordinary cited corpus heading unless its `CELORGA_RUN_ID` resolves unambiguously to a run approval, in which case it is a derived projection and is omitted as a second writable decision. Preserve the exact `Provider draft: PROVIDER:TOOL:DRAFT_ID` line and request replacements on the existing run. The CLI reuses matching pending material, supersedes older versions without falsely approving them, rejects stale decisions, and closes dedicated duplicate review runs after the canonical decision. Execution guards resolve both pending and decided authority with `celorga run approval-resolve --decision-key KEY --json`; private adapter mappings never override that result. Do not create a second heading or run to mirror a run approval.
Agents must use `celorga run block RUN_ID --reason "Specific clarification or next action"`; reasonless blocked runs are rejected because they give the reviewer nothing actionable to answer. If the run has a pending approval, leave it in `waiting-approval`. Only an independent clarification or operational blocker may add `--separate-from-approval`, and approval-shaped reasons are rejected even with that override.
Agents must complete durable runs with `celorga run complete RUN_ID --summary "What happened"`; use repeatable `--highlight` and `--next-action` flags when useful. The summary is the primary human-facing result, not a log line or a restatement of the goal.
Agents must not complete runs whose artifacts remain `review-required`. After a human decision, use `celorga run artifact-review RUN_ID ARTIFACT_ID --status reviewed|rejected --actor NAME`; for linked Org files inside the corpus, the command updates both the run snapshot and artifact metadata.
Only after a person confirms that an unfinished run's outcome was completed outside the workflow, use `celorga run complete-external RUN_ID --summary "Where or how it was completed" --actor NAME`. This explicit resolution marks unfinished workflow steps skipped and preserves pending approvals, unreviewed artifacts, and warning metadata as historical evidence; agents must not infer external completion on their own.
Use `celorga run reopen-external RUN_ID --summary "Corrected open-run outcome" --actor NAME` only to repair a run mistakenly completed externally from `waiting-approval`; it restores the same run and retained approval identities to the pending queue.
Agents and runtime adapters should record observable execution metadata with `celorga run runtime RUN_ID --provider ID --model ID` plus available `--tokens-used`, `--cost-used-usd`, or `--elapsed-seconds` values. Credentials never belong in the run.

Celorga interactive views (`celorga view create|refresh|state|action|undo|bridge --dir CORPUS`) save a refreshable daily plan in `views/ID.org2-interactive-view.json` with remembered choices and source-linked tasks. Its one action, `schedule`, is preview-first, fingerprint- and revision-guarded, and undoable only while the source is unchanged. Sandboxed HTML controls post `org2-view-intent` messages that can save choices or request previews but never apply.

Celorga Saved Views offers result-first tables and cards over canonical note/heading properties, with plain-language drafting and an advanced no-SQL filter/sort/group builder. `celorga property-view list|suggest|query|save|edit --dir CORPUS` exposes the same shared semantics. Portable `celorga:property-view:v1` definitions live in `views/`, one JSON file per view ID. Filters support regex (`matches`), date comparisons (`on`/`before`/`after`) and query-time date variables such as `{today}` and `{today-7d}`, so relative views never hard-code a date. A scoped view limits discovery before compilation. Query rows retain inherited properties, document titles, file/line and source revisions; edits create local overrides through preview-first, revision-guarded atomic source writes. IDs, built-in fields, Celorga runtime metadata, hidden paths and raw imports are read-only. See the tooling reference for the definition contract.

## Agent entry points

- [Headless server](headless-server.html): macOS CLI relay and scheduler, optional read-only Streamable HTTP corpus MCP, hash-only per-client access tokens, iOS host pairing, explicit per-host local-agent filesystem access and corpus automation ownership, user launchd service, and current failover boundaries.

## Source and specification

- https://github.com/aviaviavi/celorga
- https://github.com/aviaviavi/celorga/blob/main/spec/v0/SPEC.org
- https://github.com/aviaviavi/celorga/blob/main/spec/v0/GRAMMAR.ebnf
- https://github.com/aviaviavi/celorga/blob/main/spec/v0/PARSING.org
- https://github.com/aviaviavi/celorga/blob/main/spec/v0/canonical-ast.schema.json
- https://github.com/aviaviavi/celorga/blob/main/spec/v0/parsing-cases.json
- https://github.com/aviaviavi/celorga/blob/main/spec/v0/CONFORMANCE.org

TODO workflows: corpus defaults are celorga.json todo.sequences (an array of sequence strings), edited with todo-config show/set or Celorga Settings → General → TODO States. Files override defaults with file-local #+TODO: active | terminal sequences; use todo set --keyword STATE for exact custom states. See tooling-reference.html and language-reference.html.

- List checkbox edits: `celorga checkbox --file FILE --line N` previews `[ ] -> [-] -> [X] -> [ ]`; add `--apply` to write, and `--fix-cookies` to refresh progress cookies atomically after the marker change. `checkbox set --status unchecked|indeterminate|checked` selects a state. `checkbox fix-cookies --file FILE` previews recalculation of stale `[n/m]` and `[p%]` cookies, including empty `[/]` and `[%]` placeholders, using their innermost heading totals. The LSP exposes checkbox cycling as a code action for unsaved buffers.

- Experimental Paste as Org: default-off under Settings → General → Experimental features; Source-editor command with local HTML/plain-text conversion, optional tiny classifier, editable preview and explicit insertion. See https://celorga.io/editors-macos.html.

Celorga for iOS provides on-device fuzzy search across note titles, headings, and entry text, with previews and rendered entry/full-note navigation. No AI turn or Mac connection is needed for local lookup.

Projects: celorga project list/show/create/adopt/update uses one ordinary Org note
for a shared brief, TODO actions, color, and related chat UUIDs. Writes preview
by default; preserve preview ID/path and use --if-revision across updates.
Celorga for macOS offers project groups and linked-chat context; grouping does not
isolate permissions or provider memory. See tooling-reference.html.

Live embeds: `celorga embed resolve --target id:ID|file:relative.org --file SOURCE --dir CORPUS --json` validates portable `#+EMBED:` note/heading references read-only. Celorga offers insertion, source navigation and automatic source refresh; shared rendering bounds cycles, duplicate IDs and content. Exports never dereference embedded source; disclosure-safe publishing emits target-free omission markers.

Celorga Context → Graph shows interactive one- or two-hop neighborhoods and exact unlinked title/alias mentions. Shared `celorga roam connections` returns at most 60 nodes and 200 incoming mentions from the active corpus, excluding archives, ignored files, and symlinks. `celorga roam mention-link` previews one occurrence, requires an explicit target ID and source `--if-revision`, and writes only with `--apply`; ambiguous targets are never chosen automatically.

Browser clipping: load the unpacked `integrations/browser-clip` Chromium extension, capture an article or selection with Reading note/Read later task templates, and import its clip file in Celorga Capture → Import Browser Clip. `celorga browser-clip import` uses the same shared capture/provenance renderer as URL capture, previews first, requires destination and clip revisions for apply, keeps literal text in `views/browser-clips.org`, and preserves the immutable raw source, URL, author and browser capture time under `raw/browser/`.

Celorga opens `.canvas` files as spatial JSON Canvas boards. Files → Canvas creates or imports boards; cards support text, note/heading references, local images, groups, move/resize interactions, and editable connections. The shared `celorga canvas` CLI supplies validation, source revision guards, import/export roundtrips, and stable `id:ID` source navigation. Unknown fields remain in canonical JSON; missing or unsafe resources produce placeholders without leaving the active corpus.

## Native tooling and capability gaps

Use Celorga's native CLI by default for Org operations such as search, agenda, TODOs, links, tables, export, and validation. Prefer exposed Celorga workspace/MCP tools for operations they support; client-required effective-text reads and reviewed writes take precedence over shell access. Discover commands with `celorga agent capabilities` and `celorga COMMAND --help` before choosing a workaround. Celorga is an independent runtime: a .org file does not imply GNU Org semantics or an Emacs dependency.

Do not invoke `emacs`, `emacsclient`, batch Emacs Lisp, or an Emacs Org exporter as an implicit fallback. Do not assume Emacs is installed, probe for it, or install it for ordinary Celorga work. Use Emacs only when the user explicitly requests an Emacs-specific task. This does not prohibit other tools for work outside Celorga's scope.

If a native operation appears missing or broken, check the installed version, capabilities, and relevant help first. Distinguish a missing executable, permission restriction, or unavailable tool from a confirmed Celorga capability gap; do not bypass access or review boundaries. State the exact limitation and use a small, supported, reviewable alternative when available. Never silently substitute GNU Org behavior or execute preserved unsupported formulas or source blocks. If this is authorized Celorga development with repository access, reproduce and fix the shortcoming and add a focused regression test. Otherwise, suggest opening an issue at https://github.com/aviaviavi/celorga/issues and prepare a sanitized report with the version, command/tool, minimal input, expected and actual behavior, and workaround. Do not publish an issue or private corpus content without the user's authorization. If shell execution is unavailable, use the exposed tools and explain any remaining limitation rather than inventing command results.

Completed HTML source blocks render in the app and AI chat as live previews with expandable source. Inline scripts run and may load HTTPS libraries and data inside an opaque-origin sandbox that cannot reach the chat, corpus, local files, or app; frames size to their content unless `:height N` is given. Standalone HTML files also support interaction. Reviewed chat workspace edits accept .html, .htm, and .xhtml with SHA-bound previews and stale-write checks.
